quotes.text: Virtual bank account services that don’t open accounts in your name, such as Wise and Payoneer, aren’t supported for payouts in Japan.
Choosing a payout schedule doesn’t change how long it takes for your pending balance to become available.
Manual payouts initiated before 5 pm US/Eastern are eligible for same-day manual payouts.
When a payout fails, the status might initially show as `paid`, but then change to `failed` within 5 business days.

old_evidence.text: Your first payout might take longer, depending on your industry risk level and country of operation.
Choosing a payout schedule doesn’t change how long it takes for your pending balance to become available.
This same-day payout is limited to 10 same-day manual payouts per day, with a maximum transaction amount of 1 million GBP each.
Test payouts simulate a live payout but aren’t processed with the bank.

findings: The 2026-11-07 capture explains Stripe payouts from available balance, the successful first live payment prerequisite and typical 7–14-day initial window qualified by industry, country and risk, later schedule and settlement timing, and potential further bank delay. Dashboard dates are expected dates, and the Connect platform is routed separately (old 4-14, new 5-21).

The merchant supplies local bank details and matches payout settings currency. Supported additional settlement currencies require one account per currency and a default. Configured currencies settle without conversion and unconfigured currencies convert to the default. For eligible US businesses, payment proceeds settle in the Stripe financial account and bank information is needed for external payouts (old 1013-1033, new 1016-1036).

Business-day and calendar-day delay depend on the connected account country when a platform sets delay_days, with Brazil Pix, Boleto, debit and prepaid and Singapore PayNow exceptions. Country and payment-method timing determines balance availability from confirmation/capture, separate from payout cadence and bank credit (old 1088-1194, new 1097-1203).

Balances below country or currency minimum stay in Stripe until sufficient. A persistent negative available balance can generate a bank-account debit, so the external bank account must support credits and debits. Bank return can take up to five additional business days and apparent paid may become failed within five business days. Correct details and the next scheduled interval retry route matter, and inaccurate bank information can send funds to an unrecoverable wrong account (old 1208-1293, 1617-1625, new 1217-1302, 2976-2984).

Root index line 7 routes to Stripe index lines 539-551 and 715-721, which link the source and concept. Source lines 67-74 and concept lines 80-90 provide the reciprocal links and source/old-raw provenance. Concept lines 8-46 touch the affected timing, schedule, currency and account-type content. Adjacent specialized source routes were inspected as navigation.
substantive_changes: Same-day manual payouts now have explicit currencies, eligibility cutoffs and cap basis (old 1067-1075, new 1078-1088). US USD at standard T+2 or slower before 5 pm US/Eastern typically otherwise within one business day. GB GBP at standard T+3 or slower before 5 pm Europe/London typically otherwise within two. The new EUR row lists CH, EU, GB, MT and NO at T+3 or slower before 4 pm Europe/Copenhagen, with high-failure recipient bank rails arriving next business day and other manual payouts typically within one business day. The table specifies 10 eligible same-day payouts per day, each up to one million of the indicated currency. The May wording used business hours and did not include EUR or the explicit slower-than-standard language. Node to curl is presentation of the same create-payout endpoint.

November adds approved Stripe Capital financing payout into the selected Stripe financial account, with funds access within minutes, spending uses and default external-bank alternative, and says new Stripe users are not immediately eligible (new 1038-1044, inserted between old 1033-1035). This is finance proceeds rather than regular payment settlement.

November explicitly scopes the named futsū or tōza account requirement and exclusion of services without an account in the legal entity's name to Japan (new 1012-1014), in contrast to the May general virtual-account support with a higher-failure warning (old 1007-1011). The separately retained Japan cross-border FXYCS participation requirement is at old 488 and new 493.

The Japan settlement row now says 7 calendar days initial and 4 business days default, and the payment method table adds 5 business days for USD Bank Transfers, separate from standard ACH Debit at 4 business days (old 1154-1157 and 1181-1192, new 1162-1165 and 1189-1201).

November describes any applicable non-primary-currency multi-currency fee as charged on settlement, rather than at payout, and says certain non-primary currencies have no settlement fee. May says most non-primary-currency payouts incur fees. Both say Stripe charges no fee to initiate normal payouts (old 1017-1023 and 1627-1629, new 1020-1026 and 2986-2988).

November supplies country-specific test bank-account values for simulated successful, failed and some ineligible instant payouts, while May has the test instructions without those bank tables. Both include test debit-card fixtures. These are additions to test documentation and establish neither new live country eligibility nor bank processing (old 1283-1299, new 1292-2658, diff 2080-3447).

Most formatting differences are delimiter widths, emphasis, wording, whitespace and title revisions. Navigation changed to money-management Dashboard settings for bank details/currency, new Connect connected-account and cross-border paths, multi-currency-settlement path, dedicated payout creation and payout failure-code reference. These targets were not used as new behavior evidence (old 8-16, 1029-1033, 1065-1070, 1617-1619, new 9-21, 1032-1036, 1076-1080, 2976-2978).

answers.Q1: The 2026-11-07 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payouts describes payouts by Stripe from available balance to a bank account with matching currency and location-specific details. After the first successful live payment Stripe typically schedules the first payout to complete within 7–14 days, with country, industry and risk qualifications. Payment confirmation or capture starts settlement timing, payout schedule controls sending, and the recipient bank can take longer to make funds available. Platforms follow a separate Connect route and can set delay_days on connected accounts under local calendar- or business-day rules. Daily transfers are on business days, weekly/monthly and manual are also documented with country restrictions, and qualified US USD, GB GBP and EUR manual payouts have local cutoffs. Below-minimum balances stay in Stripe and a persistent negative balance can debit the destination bank. A failed bank return can change paid to failed within five business days. Test fixtures use test keys and simulate results without bank processing. Both captures establish the basic mechanics (old raw lines 8-16, old raw lines 1035-1125 and old raw lines 1277-1297, compared with new raw lines 9-21, new raw lines 1046-1134, new raw lines 1286-1302 and new raw lines 2976-2984). source-stripe-payouts.md captures schedules, common bank details and currency conversion but omits material settlement, failure, same-day manual and test boundaries.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payouts, source-stripe-payouts.md needs a substantive update. The 2026-11-07 capture adds approved Capital financing destination, Japan named-account and virtual-service qualifications, explicit US/GB same-day manual cutoff/eligibility language plus the named EUR regions and bank fallback, Japan’s settlement row, USD Bank Transfers at five business days, and test bank fixtures. It also clarifies when applicable non-primary-currency settlement fees apply. Preserve May 11’s general virtual account support and higher-failure caveat, earlier US/GB business-hours wording and older Japan timing row as dated claims (old raw lines 1007-1035, old raw lines 1067-1075 and old raw lines 1154-1192, compared with new raw lines 1012-1044, new raw lines 1078-1088 and new raw lines 1162-1201). Preserve the UK bank-field dependency on currency/account country and Japan manual, weekly or monthly schedule with daily unavailable in both captures. Formatting, SDK example language and moved Dashboard, Connect and API links are presentation or navigation changes. Test-only fixture additions do not evidence new live behavior, and the source should keep the original raw and reciprocal Stripe payout concept links.
